claim: Selling now costs $900 more federal tax on the $10,000 gain than selling after the one-year mark (24% vs 15%), so waiting comes out behind only if the position falls more than about 2.12% during the wait. Across all 2,470 month-long (21-trading-day) windows of the S&P 500 price index starting 2016-11-01 to 2026-08-31, the index ended lower in 30.8% of them, but fell by more than that break-even in 17.8% (20.2% for someone in the 22% bracket, whose break-even drop is 1.65%). The median window left the waiting investor $1,654 ahead, mostly from the market's rise in this period; in the worst 5% of windows waiting was at least $1,825 worse, and the worst window (starting 2020-02-21, index -33.0%) left $14,083 less.

numbers.definition: (0.24 - 0.15) x 10000: tax difference on the $10,000 gain if the price does not move.
100 x (1 - x*) with x* = (A0 - 0.15 x C) / (0.85 x V) and t = 0.24: index drop over the wait at which waiting leaves exactly as much after tax as selling now. Rounded to 3 decimals.

Number of 21-trading-day windows: (number of non-blank closes) - 21. Data: SP500 daily closes in the pinned file (2016-11-01 to 2026-09-30), blank (holiday) rows dropped; P_i = i-th close. Windows: every start i with i+21 <= last index, ratio x_i = P_(i+21)/P_i. Position V = 50000, gain G = 10000, basis C = 40000. Sell now after tax: A0 = V - t*G (t = ordinary rate). Wait: V1 = V*x_i; if V1 - C > 0 then A1 = V1 - 0.15*(V1 - C) else A1 = V1 (loss given no tax value). Difference d_i = A1 - A0.
Date of the first window start (first non-blank close).
Date of the last window start (21 trading days before the last close).

100 x (number of windows with d_i < 0) / windows_n, t = 0.24. Data: SP500 daily closes in the pinned file (2016-11-01 to 2026-09-30), blank (holiday) rows dropped; P_i = i-th close. Windows: every start i with i+21 <= last index, ratio x_i = P_(i+21)/P_i. Position V = 50000, gain G = 10000, basis C = 40000. Sell now after tax: A0 = V - t*G (t = ordinary rate). Wait: V1 = V*x_i; if V1 - C > 0 then A1 = V1 - 0.15*(V1 - C) else A1 = V1 (loss given no tax value). Difference d_i = A1 - A0. Rounded to 2 decimals.
Median of d_i over all windows (mean of the two middle values if the count is even), t = 0.24. Rounded to cents.
5th-percentile d_i, t = 0.24: sort d ascending and take the element at 0-based position floor(0.05 x (windows_n - 1)). Rounded to cents.
Minimum d_i over all windows, t = 0.24. Rounded to cents.
Start date of the window with the lowest ratio x_i.
100 x (x_i - 1) for that worst window. Rounded to 2 decimals.
100 x (number of windows with x_i < 1) / windows_n: how often the index was simply lower after 21 trading days.

assumptions: Single filer whose taxable income stays inside the 24% bracket ($105,700-$201,775 for 2026) with or without the gain; the long-term gain is then taxed at 15% (the 15% band for single filers extends to $533,400 in 2025 and is indexed upward). The 22% case uses $50,400-$105,700.
Modified AGI below $200,000, so the 3.8% net investment income tax does not apply (it would apply to both short- and long-term gain alike).
The position moves exactly with the S&P 500 price index (no dividends, no fees); a single stock is far more volatile.
About one month = 21 trading days; the investor sells at the window's closing price; no other gains or losses that year; a loss in the wait case is given no tax value (conservative).
Federal income tax only; state tax ignored.
